Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the run chase. The umpires are strolling to their positions and the Scotland Under-19 players can be seen taking their respective field positions. Qasim Khan is with the new ball to kick things off for them. Jaydn Denly and Ben McKinney to open for England Under-19. Let's play...
...RUN CHASE...

Right then, England Under-19 have 174 on the board to chase and will look forward to chasing it down and initiating their campaign with a victory. For Scotland Under-19, they need some extraordinary bowling performance to contain their counterparts. Stay tuned with us as we bring the run-chase just in a bit after a short break.

Luc Benkenstein with excellent figures of (10-0-41-3) is down for a quick chat. He says that it was a great performance from the team overall as they kept bowling on the right lines and lengths throughout. Adds that the spinners were excellent and they are happy with the total they have to chase.

On the flip side, England came up with a plan and executed it nicely. The pacers set the tone for them and the spinners got a good purchase off the deck and result, Luc Benkenstein picked a brilliant 3-fer along with his spinning mate Farhan Ahmed who also chipped in with a 3-fer with excellent economy rates. They turned the ball both ways and kept the pressure on the opposition intact. They bowled on tight lines and lengths and just didn't provide any breathing space to open the floodgates and go big and kept the game under their control for the maximum. Jaydn Denly too, joined the party at the backend of the innings. English pacers were also accurate with their plans and bowled tidy spells but they did not get enough help and yet they kept the Scottish batters tied up for runs. Sebastian Morgan was the only seamer with a wicket but the others didn't concede many.

This brings us to the end of the first innings and England Under-19 would be the happier side of the two. Scotland have posted a total of 174 runs. They started off on a sluggish note with openers Adi Hegde and Jamie Dunk. Adi Hegde ate up a lot of deliveries and sooner departed on just 3. Bahadar Esakhiel was the next to the hut in the same over without troubling the scorers. Next to the crease was the skipper Owen Gould who stitched up a sedate partnership with the opener Jamie Dunk of 40 runs. They didn't score quick runs but kept rotating the strike at times but just couldn't get enough boundaries with just a maximum throughout their innings. Jamie Dunk looked confident and just about when they were well settled and comfortable, he perished on a well-made 40 off 70 rocks. Next to depart was Uzair Ahmad. The pressure kept ticking on them and the skipper Owen Gould couldn't contain it and succumbed in the 32nd over on 48. Mackenzie Jones was looking good but he couldn't convert his start into the big score. Overall, Scotland couldn't build partnerships when needed and kept losing wickets at regular intervals which compelled them to start all over again and couldn't convert some starts to big scores.
No more participation from the injured player and there's absent hurt written against the name of Harry Armstrong.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! A soft dismissal at the end for Scotland Under-19! On a length and on off, Logan Briggs looks to block it but the ball hits the upper part of his bat. It lobs back towards Logan Briggs who makes no mistake. Scotland Under-19 end their innings for 174/9!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match formalities and we are all ready for the game to get underway. The England Under-19 players are seen taking their respective fielding positions as the umpires stroll to their marks. Adi Hegde and Jamie Dunk will open the innings for Scotland Under-19. The players can be seen getting lined up near the boundary ropes for their respective national anthems. Scotland Under-19's national anthem will be followed by England Under-19's anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree is pitchside and says the dimensions are 88m over the bowler's head and 65 each square of the wickets. Lydia joins him and she says that the pitch is similar looking to yesterday's deck and there is a bit of grass around the back of length. Adds that the West Indian spinners got a bit of help yesterday but ends up saying that many runs will be scored here.

Owen Gould the skipper of Scotland Under-19 says that they would have bowled as well as its a new wicket. Adds that they are high on confidence and really excited. Ends by saying that they will look to win this one.

Ben McKinney the skipper of England Under-19 says that the pitch might do a little bit early on and they will look to capitalise. Says that the preparations have been really good. Adds that they have played a few matches coming into this game and that momentum will help them and that they will try to enjoy our time here and play good cricket.
England Under-19 (Playing XI) - Ben McKinney (C), Jaydn Denly, Noah Thain, Hamza Shaikh, Luc Benkenstein, Charlie Allison, Dominic Kelly, Jack Carney (WK), Sebastian Morgan, Eddie Jack, Farhan Ahmed.

Scotland Under-19 (Playing XI) - Jamie Dunk, Adi Hegde, Bahadar Esakhiel, Owen Gould (C)(WK), Uzair Ahmad, Harry Armstrong, Mackenzie Jones, Ibrahim Faisal, Ruaridh Mclntyre, Logan Briggs, Qasim Khan.
TOSS - England Under-19 have won the toss and will BOWL first.

As for the Scotland Under-19, they come after two consecutive defeats against New Zealand and Nepal in the warm-ups and if they are to pull off an upset at Potchefstroom against England, their captain Owen Gould, and company will have to be at their very best. Will England kick off their campaign with a win or will Scotland err a shocker? We will see as the Toss and the team sheets are just around the corner.

England Under-19 will be entering the main phase of the tournament with a lukewarm performance in the warm-ups after getting thumped by Afghanistan and marginally winning against Pakistan. The skipper Ben McKinney will have a huge responsibility with the bat along with Hamza Shaikh and Luc Benkenstein whereas, Dominic Kelly will execute the all-rounder role. Both departments will be aiming to step up and play more responsibly.

Hello and a very warm welcome to our coverage of Match 4 of the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2024 where England Under-19 will be locking horns with Scotland Under-19 at JB Marks Oval at Potchefstroom. So brace yourself to witness an exciting European clash with us.
... MATCH DAY ...

The 2024 Under-19 World Cup is just getting started, and it is now time for match number 4, which sees two European rivals, England Under-19 and Scotland Under-19, lock horns at the JB Marks Oval in Potchefstroom. The 1998 winners, England, come into this tournament as the runners-up of the previous edition in the West Indies, whereas Scotland finished 14th out of 16 teams at that event. As part of the preparations for the event, England Under-19 took part in two warm-up games where Afghanistan defeated them in the first fixture, but they bounced back to get the better of Pakistan in the next match. Hamza Shaikh and Luc Benkenstein, who displayed good batting performances during the Quadrangular series with India A, India B, and Bangladesh, will bear the responsibility, as will skipper Ben McKinney. As far as their all-rounder department goes, Jaydn Denly and Noah Thain are the names that stand out, and the duo will be expected to contribute with both bat and ball. Eddie Jack will lead the seam attack for England, where Dominic Kelly and Sebastian Morgan will complement him. Tazeem Ali and Farhan Ahmed are the spin bowling options McKinney will have at his disposal. On the other hand, Scotland Under-19, led by Owen Gould, are coming off losses against Nepal and New Zealand in their warm-up games. Jamie Dunk, who showcased his prowess with the bat during the Europe Qualifier, holds a crucial role in their batting lineup. Bahadar Esakhiel and Uzair Ahmad will be required to make significant batting contributions if Scotland are to pull off upsets in the competition. Alec Price and Mackenzie Jones form the crux of the all-rounder contingent for the Scotts. Jones will pair with Ruaridh Mclntyre upfront with the new ball, and the onus will be on them for early breakthroughs, while spin twins Logan Briggs and Qasim Khan will hold the key in the middle phase. England Under-19 are the overwhelming favourites heading into this game. Will they start their campaign with a win? Or will it be Scotland Under-19 that springs a surprise? We shall find out.
